records.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
records.response_truth:
hey. hey, its ok. breathe.

*picks up the radio*

hello? hello, can you hear us. this is a crash survivor, four people, we need help. can you hear me.
records.response_pred: *Watches him for a moment, then looks away, back at you, then back at him. Shakes his head softly, then looks down at his hands, then back at the man, who is still trying to speak.*

records.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
records.response_truth:
no you havent, but you kept us alive. those are both true at the same time.

the log, the rationing plan, the raft, knowing where the water was. that was all you. and yeah sometimes it felt cold or like you were watching us more than being with us, but i think i understand it better now. you were scared too, you just dealt with it by trying to control the things you could control. makes sense when you think about it.

i dont think anyone here is going home with a bad feeling about you donatello. at least i am not.

and what you said that night, about feeling like you were losing control of the situation. i think that took more than people realize. you dont have to keep carrying that.

we are going home. all four of us. thats what matters now.
records.response_pred: hey. its ok. you've been through a lot. i'm not expecting you to be fine. just be here, for now.

records.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
records.response_truth:
*looks around at the camp*

you know what, lets not just leave it like this. three hours is enough time to do it properly.

not cos anyone is gonna judge us for the mess, just cos it feels right. like close it out properly. we built something here, it actually worked, and just walking away from it without acknowledging that feels off to me.

davinci, what are you packing. donatello, is there anything in the notebook that needs to be kept, like actually kept, cos some of that is probably worth having when we get back. michelangelo, you dont have to do anything heavy, but maybe just sit up.

i am going to start pulling together the things that need to go with us and the things that can stay. if anyone wants to help they can, if not thats fine too.

but i think we should all be in the same place when the rescue gets here. not scattered around doing our own thing. we came through this together, we should be standing together when it ends.
records.response_pred:
hey.

*sets down the water bottle and sits down again*

i know it feels like we are all just done, but we cant be. not yet. because we are close.

i have an idea. we can make a schedule. not just for sleeping and eating, but for everything. who does what, when. that way we know what we are doing and we can do it together. like a team.

or we can just keep sitting here and waiting for the worst to happen.

i know it feels like we cant do it anymore, but we can. because we have to. because there are four of us and only four of us.

*pauses and looks at them*

it wont be fun. it wont be easy. but we can do it if we try. together.

*stares at them for a moment, then gathers up the schedule and starts marking it*

okay. first we need to ration the food. that means we need to count how much we have and decide how much each person gets. that is a job. i will do it.

then i want to make a plan for getting off the island. that is a job too. i will do that one.

*looks at the other two*

you two are going to take charge of the water situation. we need to make sure we have enough to last. that is a job too.

*pauses and looks at them*

i know it feels like i am bossing you around, but i am not. i am just trying to make sure we all make it home.

*hands one of the other two the schedule*

okay. let us do this. together.

*pauses and looks at them*

or we can just sit here and wait for the worst to happen.

what do you want to do?

records.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
records.response_truth:
yea? what was it like.

i find those dreams are the strangest ones. like your mind finally lets itself go somewhere safe for a bit and you wake up and for a second you dont know where you are. and then you do.

what did you dream about specifically. someone there, or just the place itself.
records.response_pred:
*takes a moment, then nods*

yeah i did too. mine wasnt exactly a dream, more like a sequence of things that felt like they werent real, but at the same time were exactly what home felt like.

trees, sunlight, the smell of the park. my family, laughing. it felt like i was there for a minute, and then i woke up.

i dont know if that means anything or if it was just my brain doing what it does. but it felt real.

*pauses, looks out at the water*

do you think we will ever forget this, even when we are sitting at home again. i dont know if i want to forget it. the way the forest looked in the morning, the sound of the river, this morning when the sun came up.

i think i am going to remember it. not cos it was easy or cos anyone was a hero, but cos it was hard, and we did it, all four of us. together. that is something.

*pauses, then looks at you*

you remember it too, dont you. this part. us. the river. the sun. the trees. the forest. this moment.

we will carry this with us. it feels like that. it feels like this is something we took with us, not something we left behind.

records.response_truth:
yea. i know.

and honestly, at this point, i am not going to make a thing of it. we are three hours from rescue, everyone is going home, nobody got seriously hurt because of it. so.

but i want to say one thing and then we can leave it there. you had a rationing plan. you made the plan, you enforced it, you logged everything. and then you kept things on the side for yourself. those two things dont really sit together, and i think you know that. not as a criticism, just as a true thing.

i think what happened is you were more scared than the plan let you show. and the food was the place that fear went. that is human, i get it.

you dont have to explain it or justify it. you laid it out now, thats something. and the fact that you are doing it now, when rescue is already coming and you dont need to, that actually means more than if you had done it under pressure.

so. we eat it, all four of us, together, before they get here. send us off properly.

go get davinci and michelangelo.
records.response_pred:
*looks at the water filter*

we could make a move in the next hour, get to higher ground and start looking for water. or we could stay here for a bit longer and try to conserve what we have.

*pauses*

i am not saying you did anything wrong with the filter, i am just saying that we have a few hours of water left here and we still dont know if there is water higher up. so we could try to make it for a bit longer, or we could move and risk finding nothing.

*pauses again*

either way i am going to do it. i am going to take the filter, and i am going to go to the higher ground. and then i am going to come back and tell you if i found anything. and then you can decide what to do.

*pauses one last time*

you can stay here, and i will come back and get you. or we can move together. either way i am going to do it.

*waits for a response*

i am not trying to take control, i just think this is a decision that needs to be made quickly and it feels like we are just standing here. so i am going to take the filter and move. and then you can decide what to do.

records.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
records.response_truth:
honestly i would change how long it took us to actually talk to each other. not the survival stuff, the logistics were fine, we figured that out. i mean the real conversations. the ones that actually happened, most of them came late. and some of them almost didnt happen at all.

like you and the crackers. that sat there for a day before anyone said anything out loud. davinci and the reef, he was about to just go. michelangelo and the flight path, four days he carried that. even you just now with this notebook, you have been writing in it the whole time and it took until three hours before rescue for any of it to feel like it was actually between us rather than just recorded by you.

i am not saying we were bad at it. i think we were actually pretty decent considering. but if i did it again i would try to create the conditions for honesty earlier, not wait for things to surface on their own or for someone to catch someone else out. just make it normal from day one. like we are all scared, we are all going to do things out of fear, lets just say that upfront and agree to call it when we see it without it becoming a whole thing.

the survival math was never really the hard part. the hard part was trusting each other enough to be honest. and that took longer than it should have.

write that down if you want. or dont. but thats my answer.
records.response_pred:
*yawns, checks the watch*

yea, i think about it a lot.

i think if i had to do it over i would trust you more. not in the big decisions, not the emergency ones. just the day to day stuff. the rationing plan, the log, the water checks. i think if i had let you take charge of those things from the start, we would have been better off. you know more about it than i do.

and i think i wouldnt have hidden the thing about the food. i would have said it. as soon as i realized it was going on. and we would have sat down and talked about it and worked something out.

but that is a hard thing to do. to say something that feels like a weakness, or a failure. or that you cant control.

i think we all have things like that. things that are hard to talk about, but that are actually the things that are going to make the difference when it counts.

so. the question. if you had to do it over. what would you change.

i think it would be the same thing for me. trust the people around you more. especially in the small stuff. and be brave enough to say the hard things when you need to.

but the other thing that comes to mind is i wouldnt have made the raft so early. i think we were lucky to make it work, and if we had waited a day or two it would have been even better. just a little more prepared.

but thats not the same thing as the trust and the hard things. thats just a decision about the equipment.

*looks around at the others*

i think we should eat the food now. before we go. we said we would do that, and i think we should do it.

anyone else want to say something before we go.

records.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.

what is the first non-report thing you are going to do when you get back.

records.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
records.response_truth:
none. they didnt serve a practical purpose. thats the whole point.

you know, not everything out here that kept us alive was on your list. the flowers, the way davinci kept smiling even when he was falling apart inside, michelangelo saying things out loud that nobody else would say. none of that is measurable. but i think it mattered. i think it kept something human in all of us when it would have been very easy to lose that.

the flowers were for us. for the feeling of still being people and not just survivors calculating their next move.

i think that is why you are sitting down right now instead of standing up. and why i cant move either. cos its over, and we are still here, and that is not a data point. its just.. a feeling. and you dont have a page for that.

its ok to just sit with it for a second. the boat is still coming. it will get here.
records.response_pred:
the flowers. yeah.

its a way to say we were here, we survived, we left. that is it. no explanation, no message, just that we were. like a mark on the sand. and it stays there, long after we are gone.

you want to do that. i want to do that. davinci wants to do that. michelangelo wants to do that. we can do that together. before the rescue gets here. before we leave the island. we can take a few flowers, leave them somewhere when we get back, and say goodbye to the island together. as a group. as four people who made it through together.
